- **self**: UX research strategy and method selection (22/5)

## Definitions

- [statement] Treat method maps as adaptable guidance: classifications are not rigid, and research questions, organizational resources, and stakeholder needs shape the approach. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/which-ux-research-methods/ · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://www.userinterviews.com/ux-research-field-guide-chapter/how-to-choose-a-research-method

## How it works

- [statement] NN/g recommends considering context of product use when choosing a method: natural use prioritizes realism but offers less control over topics, while scripted use focuses the study on selected product areas. (low confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/which-ux-research-methods/ · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection
- [statement] Plan inclusive recruitment, access needs, and informed consent explicitly; GOV.UK recommends including varied users, disabled users, and people who need support when the service has a broad audience. (medium confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research/plan-user-research-for-your-service · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research/plan-round-of-user-research
- [statement] Triangulation can add time and can encourage confirmation bias when researchers select supporting data and ignore disconfirming evidence. Dscout recommends beginning triangulation before conclusions harden or involving a partner to check bias. (low confidence) — https://dscout.com/people-nerds/triangulate-user-research · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Scale research effort to the risk, consequences, and reversibility of the decision as well as research cost; expensive choices justify stronger triangulation than simple, easily reversible choices. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/triangulation-better-research-results-using-multiple-ux-methods/ · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://enterprisearchitecture.harvard.edu/user-research-methods-and-recommendations

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Use generative research to explore needs and opportunities, and evaluative research to assess how well a proposed or existing solution meets user needs; these describe research purposes rather than a mandatory sequence of methods. (medium confidence) — https://www.userinterviews.com/ux-research-field-guide-chapter/how-to-choose-a-research-method · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://enterprisearchitecture.harvard.edu/user-research-methods-and-recommendations, https://www.nngroup.com/articles/which-ux-research-methods/
- [statement] Synthetic-user output should be treated as model-generated hypotheses or supplementary material rather than observations from human participants; it cannot establish human experience without research with people. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/synthetic-users/ · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://interactions.acm.org/archive/view/january-february-2026/the-challenges-of-synthetic-users-in-ux-research
- [statement] Treat method taxonomies as guides rather than rigid classifications: a method can collect more than one type of evidence or serve different objectives depending on the study design. (low confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/which-ux-research-methods/ · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection
- [statement] When methods disagree, investigate study questions and conduct before choosing an interpretation. Check participant groups, tasks, logistics, and analysis; conflicting results can motivate further research rather than automatic preference for one data type. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/interpreting-research-findings/ · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://dscout.com/people-nerds/triangulate-user-research

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Start with the decision and the assumptions that need testing. Agree actionable research questions before choosing methods, and select activities that give reliable answers within the available time, effort, and cost. (medium confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research/plan-user-research-for-your-service · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research/plan-round-of-user-research
- [statement] Attitudinal research addresses reported beliefs and perceptions; behavioral research addresses actions. Select the evidence type that matches the question, and do not treat stated intentions as proof of future behavior. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/which-ux-research-methods/ · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://www.userinterviews.com/ux-research-field-guide-chapter/how-to-choose-a-research-method
- [statement] Qualitative approaches are suited to exploring why or how a problem occurs and how it might be fixed; quantitative approaches are suited to questions about how many, how much, or how often. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/which-ux-research-methods/ · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://www.userinterviews.com/ux-research-field-guide-chapter/how-to-choose-a-research-method, https://enterprisearchitecture.harvard.edu/user-research-methods-and-recommendations
- [statement] A research plan should identify questions and objectives, target user groups, research activities, recruitment, and the decisions each round will support; prepare the highest-priority rounds and revise the plan as learning develops. (medium confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research/plan-user-research-for-your-service · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research/plan-round-of-user-research
- [statement] Plan time for analysis and agree how findings will enter team decisions; collecting session data alone does not complete the research plan. (medium confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research/plan-round-of-user-research · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research/plan-user-research-for-your-service
- [statement] Triangulation combines complementary evidence or analytical perspectives on a question. Quantitative findings can indicate the extent of an issue while qualitative evidence helps explain it; evidence from one approach can guide a follow-up approach. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/triangulation-better-research-results-using-multiple-ux-methods/ · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://maze.co/blog/mixed-methods-research/
- [statement] Using several methods does not automatically remove bias or resolve inconsistency: researchers must preserve methodological distinctions, check comparability, and address divergent interpretations. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9714985/ · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://atlasti.com/guides/the-guide-to-mixed-methods-research/triangulation-in-mixed-methods-research
- [statement] Review existing evidence before commissioning new research: a decision may already be informed by available data, and triangulation can include existing analytics or customer-satisfaction information. (medium confidence) — https://www.userinterviews.com/ux-research-field-guide-chapter/how-to-choose-a-research-method · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/triangulation-better-research-results-using-multiple-ux-methods/
- [statement] Distinguish attitudinal evidence about what people say, think, or feel from behavioral evidence about what they do. Self-reported beliefs are limited by what participants know and are willing to report. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/which-ux-research-methods/ · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://enterprisearchitecture.harvard.edu/user-research-methods-and-recommendations
- [statement] For each research round, plan participant inclusion and access needs, recruitment budget, informed consent, recording or note-taking responsibilities, and time for analysis. (low confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research/plan-round-of-user-research · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection
- [statement] Plan how findings will enter team decisions and where outputs will be stored and shared. Research scheduling should stay aligned with the team’s priorities and ability to act on findings. (low confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research/plan-user-research-for-your-service · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection
- [statement] Triangulation combines multiple sources or approaches to examine a question from different viewpoints. It can use complementary qualitative and quantitative evidence, existing records, or separate researcher analyses; it does not require a fixed number of methods. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/triangulation-better-research-results-using-multiple-ux-methods/ · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://dscout.com/people-nerds/triangulate-user-research
- [statement] NN/g’s 2024 guidance recommends treating synthetic-user outputs as hypotheses to test with real people, and explicitly identifying their origin. They should not be presented as findings from human participants or used to replace real-user research. (low confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/synthetic-users/ · keywords: UX research strategy and method selection
